comments.content: Now that this body runs on the SNAPSHOT pool instead of synchronously inside the cluster-state callback that scheduled it, the entry lookup on the next line (`SnapshotsInProgress.get(clusterService.state()).snapshot(snapshot)`) can legitimately return `null` (`SnapshotsInProgress#snapshot` is `@Nullable`): the entry may have been removed/aborted (e.g. a delete request for a snapshot with no shard work, or a state change after a master failover) between submission and execution. `entry.failure()` would then NPE, which only surfaces later as an `unexpected failure finalizing ...` assertion/error and a finalization failure with `ShardGenerations.EMPTY`. Please handle the missing entry explicitly instead of dereferencing it.

On executor shutdown `handleFinalizationFailure` -> `removeFailedSnapshotFromClusterState` submits a cluster state update task (whose `clusterStateProcessed` calls `runNextQueuedOperation` -> `finalizeSnapshotEntry`, which submits to the same shut-down SNAPSHOT executor). During shutdown these submissions are rejected again, so every queued finalization re-enters `onRejection`/`handleFinalizationFailure` and the cleanup can never actually complete (and the cluster state update may itself be rejected by the shutting-down master service). Consider just logging the rejection and leaving the cleanup to the normal shutdown/shutdown-listener handling rather than driving the failure path off a shut-down executor.

This write used to be queued on the repository executor; it is now executed inline on the SNAPSHOT thread, while the global/index metadata writes above are still queued on that same SNAPSHOT executor. Since (per the new assertion at the top of this method) the whole finalization orchestration now also occupies a SNAPSHOT thread while it waits for those queued sub-tasks, each concurrent finalization holds one SNAPSHOT thread until its own sub-tasks get a thread. With several repositories finalizing at once this can exhaust the (bounded max) SNAPSHOT pool and stall the very metadata writes the finalization is waiting for, in addition to keeping the thread blocked on this IO. Please consider keeping the write on the executor as before, or documenting why blocking the SNAPSHOT thread here is safe.
